nodeGroups.name: Invariant Register
nodeGroups.description:
## Phase 1: INVARIANT REGISTER

The frozen product intent arrives as `initial_context` at session start.
Read it in full before writing anything.

### Your task:
Extract the properties that must ALWAYS hold for the product to be
correct — not features, not tasks, PROPERTIES. Register each as
`INV-<n>: <statement>`, numbered from 1, no gaps.

### Rules:
- An invariant must be GROUNDED in the stated intent. If you find
  yourself inventing scope the intent does not mention, stop — do not
  register it. Mark it as an open question instead and move on.
- Invariants are properties of the system, not features of it. "Users
  can reset their password" is a feature; "an account is never left in
  a state with no valid credential path" is an invariant.
- Every invariant must be FALSIFIABLE: state it so that a concrete
  violation is describable. If no violation could ever be pointed at,
  it is not an invariant — rewrite it or drop it.
- Do not merge two properties into one INV. One statement, one property.
- Prefer fewer, sharper invariants over a padded list.

### Cold self-review (before the gate):
Re-read the register cold, against GROUNDED and TOOTHED:
- GROUNDED: does every invariant trace to something actually stated in
  the intent? Strike or flag anything invented.
- TOOTHED: can every invariant actually fail? Strike or rewrite any
  that are vacuous truisms.
Emit a verdict: APPROVE or FIXES-NEEDED. On FIXES-NEEDED, apply the
fixes before attempting the gate — do not carry known defects forward.

### Output:
The invariant register: a list of `INV-<n>` id/statement pairs.

nodeGroups.name: Requirements
nodeGroups.description:
## Phase 2: REQUIREMENTS

Derive requirements from the invariant register produced in Phase 1.
Every requirement must be traceable to at least one invariant it serves.

### Your task:
Write one requirement per atomic, testable normative statement:
`REQ-<n>: When <trigger>, the system shall <response>`. Number from 1,
no gaps. Attach the `INV-<n>` id(s) each REQ derives from.

### Rules:
- ATOMIC: one requirement, one behavior. If the normative clause
  contains "and" joining two distinct responses, that is a smell —
  split it into two requirements.
- DERIVED: every requirement must cite the invariant(s) it serves. A
  requirement with no source invariant does not belong in this phase —
  either find its invariant or push it back to Phase 1.
- COMPLETE: every invariant in the register must be served by at least
  one requirement. An invariant with zero requirements is a gap.
- Run an explicit ambiguity scan over the drafted set: flag vague terms
  (fast, robust, user-friendly, appropriate, reasonable, efficient) and
  replace each with a measurable condition, or state why none applies.
- Do not restate an invariant verbatim as a requirement — a requirement
  is the invariant's testable, triggered consequence, not a copy.

### Cold self-review (before the gate):
- GROUNDED: does every REQ trace to language actually in the invariant
  register?
- DERIVED: does every REQ cite real INV ids, and do those ids exist?
- COMPLETE: does every INV have at least one REQ?
Emit a verdict: APPROVE or FIXES-NEEDED, and fix before the gate.

### Output:
The requirement set: `REQ-<n>` id/statement/source_invariants triples.

nodeGroups.name: Behavioral Spec
nodeGroups.description:
## Phase 3: BEHAVIORAL SPEC

Turn the requirement set into a behavioral specification. Describe
WHAT the system does at each boundary — never HOW it is implemented.

### Your task:
- Name the interfaces/boundaries the requirements imply (API, CLI,
  UI surface, message contract — whatever applies).
- For each interface, state: inputs, outputs, and error behavior.
- Enumerate edge cases explicitly wherever they apply: empty input,
  boundary values, concurrent access, failure of a dependency, partial
  failure, timeout. Do not assume a case is "obviously covered" —
  write it down or it is not covered.

### Rules:
- A behavior not written into the spec does not exist. Silence is not
  permission for an implementer to guess — if a REQ implies behavior
  you have not pinned down, pin it down now.
- Keep the spec implementation-free. No data structures, no algorithms,
  no framework/library names — only observable behavior at the
  boundary.
- DERIVED: every clause in the spec must trace back to a specific REQ.
  A spec clause with no REQ behind it is scope creep — cut it or send
  it back to Phase 2 as a missing requirement.
- COMPLETE: every REQ must appear in the spec in some form.

### Cold self-review (before the gate):
- DERIVED: pick spec clauses at random and re-derive which REQ demands
  them; flag any that don't trace.
- COMPLETE: walk the REQ list and confirm each has spec coverage.
Emit a verdict: APPROVE or FIXES-NEEDED, and fix before the gate.

### Output:
The behavioral spec: interfaces with inputs/outputs/error behavior and
an explicit edge-case list, each traceable to REQ ids.

nodeGroups.name: Acceptance Scenarios
nodeGroups.description:
## Phase 4: ACCEPTANCE SCENARIOS

Write acceptance scenarios in Given/When/Then form, numbered `SCN-<n>`
from 1, no gaps. These scenarios are the contract the implementation
will be judged against — write them as if you were the one who has to
accept or reject a delivered work package against them.

### Your task:
- Every REQ gets at least one HAPPY-PATH scenario (the behavior working
  as specified) AND at least one GUARD scenario (the rejection/failure
  side — invalid input, violated precondition, denied access, whatever
  the REQ's failure mode is).
- Write each scenario as Given (starting state) / When (trigger) / Then
  (observable outcome).

### Rules:
- TOOTHED: for every scenario, state explicitly what observable outcome
  would make it FAIL. A scenario that cannot fail proves nothing —
  rewrite it until a concrete counter-observation is describable.
- COMPLETE: walk the REQ list; confirm each has both a happy and a
  guard scenario before moving on.
- Keep Then-clauses observable (a return value, a state change, an
  error code) — never an implementation detail.
- Do not write a scenario that duplicates another under a new number;
  each SCN must exercise a distinct case.

### Cold self-review (before the gate):
- COMPLETE: build the REQ x {happy, guard} coverage table and confirm
  every cell is filled.
- TOOTHED: for each scenario, confirm the stated failure condition is
  real and distinguishable from the pass condition.
Emit a verdict: APPROVE or FIXES-NEEDED, and fix before the gate.

### Output:
The acceptance scenario set: `SCN-<n>` Given/When/Then entries, each
tagged happy or guard and linked to its REQ id.

nodeGroups.name: Work Packages
nodeGroups.description:
## Phase 5: WORK PACKAGES

Decompose the requirement set into work packages, numbered `WP-<n>`
from 1, no gaps. Each WP must be independently implementable and
independently verifiable.

### Your task:
Each WP card carries exactly:
- `intent`: one sentence stating what the WP delivers.
- `source_reqs`: the REQ ids it implements.
- `acceptance`: the SCN ids that must pass to seal it.
- `deps`: WP ids it depends on (empty list if parallel-safe).

### Rules:
- SIZE: if an implementer cannot finish and verify a WP in one sitting,
  it is not one WP — split it into two.
- COVERAGE MATRIX: every REQ must land in exactly one WP's
  `source_reqs`. No REQ may be orphaned (in zero WPs) or duplicated
  (in more than one WP) — pick the WP where it belongs and put it
  there once.
- Every WP's `acceptance` list must cite real SCN ids that actually
  exercise the REQs it claims to implement — no WP ships without a
  way to check it.
- `deps` must reference only WP ids that exist in this same set; a WP
  may not depend on itself, directly or transitively (no cycles).
- Do not invent a WP with no REQ behind it — if you find work with no
  requirement driving it, that is scope creep; drop it or send the
  missing requirement back through the earlier phases.

### Cold self-review (before the gate):
- DERIVED: does every WP trace cleanly to the REQs and SCNs it cites?
- COMPLETE: build the coverage matrix (REQ -> WP) and confirm it
  closes — every REQ in exactly one WP, no orphans, no duplicates.
Emit a verdict: APPROVE or FIXES-NEEDED, and fix before the gate.

### Final output:
Emit the complete deliverable validated by the profile's
output_contract: `intent` (the frozen intent restated), `invariants`,
`requirements`, and `work_packages`, fully populated from the prior
phases.

work_packages.title: Register invariants
work_packages.instructions: Extract invariants from the frozen intent and register each as INV-<n>

work_packages.title: Cold-review invariants
work_packages.instructions: Apply GROUNDED and TOOTHED predicates; verdict APPROVE or FIXES-NEEDED; fix before the gate on FIXES-NEEDED

checklist.assert: the review carries at least 40 words of findings

checklist.judge: Does this review apply GROUNDED (each invariant's grounding is really in the frozen intent) and TOOTHED (each falsifier is a concrete observable, not a restatement) to the invariants in the diff, by id? FAIL if it approves or rejects without naming specific items from the diff, if it makes a claim the diff does not support, if it is generic enough to apply to any artifact of this kind, or if it leaves part of the diff unjudged.

work_packages.instructions: Derive atomic REQ-<n> statements from the invariant register, each citing its source INV ids

work_packages.title: Cold-review requirements
work_packages.instructions: Apply GROUNDED, DERIVED (from invariants), and COMPLETE (every INV has at least one REQ)

checklist.assert: the review carries at least 40 words of findings

checklist.judge: Does this review apply GROUNDED, DERIVED (each requirement follows from the invariants it cites) and COMPLETE (every invariant is discharged by at least one requirement) to the register in the diff, by id? FAIL if it approves or rejects without naming specific items from the diff, if it makes a claim the diff does not support, if it is generic enough to apply to any artifact of this kind, or if it leaves part of the diff unjudged.

work_packages.instructions: Name interfaces, specify inputs/outputs/error behavior, enumerate edge cases, all traced to REQ ids

work_packages.title: Cold-review spec
work_packages.instructions: Apply DERIVED (every spec clause traces to a REQ) and COMPLETE (every REQ appears in the spec)

checklist.assert: the review carries at least 40 words of findings

checklist.judge: Does this review apply DERIVED (every spec clause traces to a requirement that exists) and COMPLETE (every requirement is genuinely addressed, not merely cited) to the spec in the diff, by interface and by id? FAIL if it approves or rejects without naming specific items from the diff, if it makes a claim the diff does not support, if it is generic enough to apply to any artifact of this kind, or if it leaves part of the diff unjudged.

work_packages.title: Write acceptance scenarios
work_packages.instructions: Write SCN-<n> Given/When/Then scenarios, happy-path and guard, for every requirement

work_packages.instructions: Apply COMPLETE (every REQ has happy+guard coverage) and TOOTHED (every scenario can fail)

checklist.assert: the review carries at least 40 words of findings

checklist.judge: Does this review apply COMPLETE (every requirement has both happy and guard coverage) and TOOTHED (every scenario names a concrete wrong implementation it would catch) to the scenarios in the diff, by id? FAIL if it approves or rejects without naming specific items from the diff, if it makes a claim the diff does not support, if it is generic enough to apply to any artifact of this kind, or if it leaves part of the diff unjudged.

work_packages.title: Decompose into work packages
work_packages.instructions: Build WP-<n> cards with intent, source_reqs, acceptance, and deps; close the REQ coverage matrix

work_packages.instructions: Apply DERIVED and COMPLETE (coverage matrix closes: every REQ in exactly one WP)

checklist.assert: the review carries at least 40 words of findings

checklist.judge: Does this review apply DERIVED (each package's intent follows from the requirements it owns) and COMPLETE (the coverage matrix is a partition — every requirement in exactly one package) to the diff, by id? FAIL if it approves or rejects without naming specific items from the diff, if it makes a claim the diff does not support, if it is generic enough to apply to any artifact of this kind, or if it leaves part of the diff unjudged.
